answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to hold the sable of valid state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting specific memory indices; failure to return data matching the yarrow-like consistency of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. Each anchor of logic must reside on a unique hardware bus to prevent pooling. Honest participants pay 120 watts for status; fakes pay 120,000 watts, rendering mass-identity farms infeasible.
